column1: # peer-tiers.tsv — THE roster. One maintenance tier per peer, all 46, machine-readable.
#   The tier policy existed in CONFORMANCE-MATRIX.md §4 as prose and drifted: §4 named 17
#   peers while the cohort had grown to 46, so "re-run Tier-1" had no unambiguous meaning and
#   every re-pin turned into a full 45-peer census. This file is the single canonical home for
#   the assignment; §4 explains it, this defines it, and the tooling reads it.
# MAINTENANCE TIER != LANDSCAPE TIER. research/LANDSCAPE.md has its own tiers 1-5 which
#   classify the LANGUAGE LANDSCAPE (major platform ... functional/niche) and answer "what is
#   worth building". These answer "how often does this peer get re-measured". They are
#   deliberately spelled M1/M2/M3 so the two can never be confused again.
# WHAT A TIER MEANS (cadence only — a tier NEVER changes whether a peer may be published;
#   M1           lockstep. Re-run on EVERY oracle re-pin; must reach 0-FAIL before the re-pin
#                is considered landed. This is the gate.
#   M2           priority catch-up. Re-run once M1 has converged.
#   M3           on-demand. Re-run with spare capacity, before a release, or on an adopter ask.
#   probe        paradigm/substrate probe. Re-measured when its own axis is touched, or before
#                a release. Real peers, but not what the cadence is for.
#   exploratory  NOT a deployable peer (CONFORMANCE-MATRIX.md §1 ‡). Never gates anything.
# last_measured_pin is the oracle commit a peer's CURRENT recorded verdict was measured at.
#   A peer whose pin != tools/oracle-pin.env `ref` is STALE — a documented, tracked state, not
#   a failure. `tools/tier-status.py` reports it; the census updates it.
# spec_pin is the SPEC revision this peer was last SWEPT to — a different fact from
#   last_measured_pin, which is the ORACLE. Added 2026-09-16 at the request of
#   entity-system-conformance, whose per-peer verdicts consume it (their ADR-0003 §7.3: a
#   verdict records the peer's identity, not its name).
#   `unknown` IS A VALUE AND A BLANK IS AN ERROR. They are different claims — an empty cell
#   reads as "not applicable" to one reader and "nobody has established this" to another —
#   WHY IT IS HERE AND NOT IN profile.toml: every peer's [spec] table already declares
#   `v7_version_pinned`, and conformance measured it before asking — present on 24 of 46,
#   five distinct v7-era values, three peers carrying the free-text "v0.8.0 / V8", and 0 of
#   46 mentioning 0.8.2 while the cohort sat at 0.8.2.25. A STALE field is worse than an
#   absent one: it parses, it is plausible, and nothing in the path goes red. So this column
#   ships with a WRITER (the sweep) and a GATE, which is the half that was missing.
# Columns: peer <TAB> tier <TAB> last_measured_pin <TAB> spec_pin <TAB> note
# FIVE TOOLS PARSE THIS FILE. Inserting spec_pin at index 3 MOVED `note` from 3 to 4, and
#   exactly one reader indexed it positionally (tools/tier-status.py, fixed in the same
#   commit) — it would have displayed the spec pin as the note with nothing going red.
#   tools/arc-probe/run-mint-floor.sh ($1), tools/spec-pin-gate.py (BY HEADER NAME — it must
#   read this file as it stood at an arbitrary older commit, where index 3 is the note).
#   Audit every reader's EXTRACTION before moving a column here; `grep -rn peer-tiers` finds
#   the readers and says nothing about how they parse.
